Badr's warriors and angels are ranked the best; Gabriel came armed; Badr men in other reports: a widow's remarriage after childbirth, sacrifice meat after three days, Az-Zubair's spear.
Reports naming Badr warriors: Ubada's pledge, Abu Hudhaifa adopting Salim, a wedding lament for a Badr father, angels avoiding dogs and pictures, drunk Hamza maiming Ali's camels, Hafsa's remarriage.

Reports naming Badr warriors: spending on family as charity, Gabriel offering five prayers at fixed hours, al-Baqara's last two verses, renting fields, Bahrain's jizya, fear of wealth, sparing house snakes.
Abbas's ransom is not waived; a foe professing Islam must be spared; Abu Jahl dies; Badr warriors' stipends and booty shares; the first civil strife leaves none of them alive.
Both tribes fight; Bani An-Nadir are exiled; when Bani Quraiza fight again their men are killed, their women, children and property shared out; al-Hashr is Surat an-Nadir; An-Nadir's palms burnt.
Asked to judge Ali and Abbas over Bani An-Nadir's fai, Umar cites the Prophet: prophets' property is not inherited but given in charity; Abu Bakr answers Fatima and Abbas likewise.
The Prophet asks who will kill Ka'b bin al-Ashraf; Muhammad bin Maslama does so by a ruse; Abdullah bin Atik enters Abu Rafi's castle at night and kills him.
Gabriel comes armed at Uhud; years later the Prophet prays over its martyrs and fears worldly rivalry; archers leave their post for booty, seventy fall, and Abu Sufyan taunts them.
Abdur-Rahman and Khabbab recall Mus'ab's short shroud; promised Paradise, a man drops his dates and fights till martyred; Anas bin an-Nadr's over eighty wounds; verse 33:23 on keeping the covenant.
Verses on the split over those who turned back at Uhud and two clans that nearly faltered; Jabir, his father martyred there, marries a matron; the father's debt is paid.
At Uhud two men in white fight for the Prophet; Sa'd shoots, honoured with 'my father and mother'; Talha and Sa'd alone remain; Abu Talha shields him; women carry water.
At Satan's cry Muslims turn on each other, killing Hudhaifa's father; Ibn Umar says Allah forgave Uthman's flight; the archers retreat, the Apostle calling them back; slumber overtakes Abu Talha.
The Prophet curses certain men, among them Safwan bin Umaiya, Suhail bin Amr and al-Harith bin Hisham, in the morning prayer, and then the verse 'Not for you' comes down.
Um Salit carried water skins at Uhud; Wahshi tells how he speared Hamza and later Musailamah; Allah's wrath on those who wounded the Prophet; Fatima stops his bleeding with ashes.
Seventy go after the pagans following Uhud; the Ansar lost seventy martyrs there; Uhud's dead are buried unwashed, two to a sheet; the Prophet's dream of a broken sword.
Mus'ab's short shroud; the Prophet calls Uhud a mountain that loves us and makes Medina a sanctuary as Abraham did Mecca; he prays over Uhud's martyrs and fears worldly rivalry.
Asim bin Thabit's scouts are surrounded; Asim falls, Khubaib, sold in Mecca, prays two rak'at before Abu Sirwa' kills him, and wasps guard Asim's body.
Seventy reciters are treacherously killed at Bir Ma'una, including Haram and Amir bin Fuhaira; a later-cancelled verse speaks for them; the Prophet says Qunut against the tribes for a month.
Emigrants and Ansar dig the trench hungry as the Prophet carries earth and asks Allah's forgiveness for them; Jabir's meal feeds a thousand, and Ibn Umar fights aged fifteen.
When people differ over the caliphate and Muawiya claims a greater right to it, Ibn Umar holds back his reply for fear of causing division and bloodshed.
The Prophet says Muslims will now attack the clans, not be attacked; Asr is delayed past sunset, Az-Zubair is called his disciple, and Allah alone defeated the clans.
Gabriel sends the Prophet against Banu Qurayzah, whom Sa'd bin Mu'adh judges: warriors killed, offspring captive; Sa'd dies of his wound, and Hassan is told to abuse them in verse.
On the Dhat-ur-Riqa and Najd expeditions the Prophet leads the Fear Prayer with two batches in turn, and spares a bedouin who seized his sword as he slept.
On the Banu al-Mustaliq expedition men holding Arab captives ask about coitus interruptus; the Prophet says it is better not to, for every soul destined to exist will exist.
On the Najd expedition a bedouin draws the sleeping Prophet's sword and asks who will save him; the Prophet says 'Allah', and does not punish him.
During the Anmar expedition the Prophet offers voluntary prayers on his mount, facing east.
Aisha tells how, left behind by the army, she was slandered until revelation declared her innocent; further reports concern Ali's silence, her fainting at the news, and Hassan's part.
One rainy night in the year of al-Hudaybiya, the Prophet relays Allah's word: whoever credits rain to Allah's mercy believes in Him, and whoever credits a star disbelieves in Him.
The Prophet's four Umrahs include al-Hudaybiya, where a dried well refills and water flows from his fingers for the 1300 to 1500 men whose pledge al-Bara calls the true victory.
A report from Mirdas al-Aslami, who pledged under the Tree: the pious will pass away one after another, leaving worthless dregs to whom Allah pays no attention.
Setting out with 1300 to 1500 companions, the Prophet takes Ihram; Ka'b shaves his lice-ridden head for a ransom, Umar provides for a pledger's daughter, and the Tree is forgotten.
Pledgers under the Tree say they pledged for death, the pledge verse 48:1 refers to, and report the Prophet on charity, Friday prayer and donkey meat; one rules on witr.
Marching for Umrah, the Prophet consults on Quraysh barring him and accepts Suhail's term to return their men; emigrant women are tested, and the 'manifest victory' sura is revealed.
If barred from the Ka'bah, Ibn Umar will do as the Prophet did when Quraysh barred him, sacrifice and shave; he pledged under the Tree before Umar did.
When the Prophet performs Umrah, making Tawaf, praying and going between Safa and Marwa, his companions guard him against the people of Mecca.
Back from Siffin, Sahl bin Hunaif recalls wanting to refuse the Prophet's order on the day of Abu Jandal; lice-ridden Ka'b is told to shave and pay a ransom.
People of Ukl and Uraina accept Islam, then revert, kill the Prophet's shepherd and drive off the camels; caught, their eyes are branded and hands and legs cut off.
Salama bin al-Akwa chases the Ghatafan raiders who seized the Prophet's camels at Dhi-Qarad, recovers them with his arrows, and is told by the Prophet to forgive them.
At Khaibar, Amir bin al-Akwa dies by his own blade yet earns a double reward; the Prophet attacks at dawn, forbids donkey meat, and frees and marries the captive Safiya.
A fierce fighter the Prophet says is of Hell kills himself; the Prophet bids the army lower their voices, heals Salama's wound, and gives Ali the flag for Khaibar's conquest.
